perimenopausal-and-menopausal-women-work.core: Posted in last 7 days Perimenopausal & Menopausal Women - Workplace Support Experiences MENOPAUSE IN THE WORKPLACE: I WANT TO HEAR FROM WOMEN Are women genuinely feeling supported through perimenopause and menopause in the workplace? I'm currently developing an article to release from Becoming Her, exploring women's real experiences of menopause at work, and I would value your contribution. We often hear the statistics about menopause, career disruption, workplace challenges and women leaving employment. But what are women actually experiencing? Are managers having supportive conversations? Are workplaces making meaningful adjustments? Are women feeling understood, or are many still navigating this stage of life in silence? And importantly, what are some employers getting right? I'm inviting women who have experienced perimenopause or menopause during their working lives to share their perspectives. I'd particularly like to understand: Did you feel comfortable discussing menopause at work? Did symptoms affect your confidence, wellbeing or career decisions? What support, if any, did your employer provide? Were your manager and colleagues understanding? What could your workplace have done differently? What examples of positive workplace support would you like others to learn from? Your contribution will be completely anonymous. No names, employers or identifying details will be published. Personal experiences or quotations will only be included with your permission. I'm interested in hearing all perspectives, including positive experiences, challenges and opportunities for improvement. This isn't about criticising employers. It's about learning from women's experiences and understanding what meaningful workplace support really looks like. My intention is to bring these experiences together in an article that encourages greater awareness, understanding and practical action. WOULD YOU BE WILLING TO CONTRIBUTE? I've preparing a short questionnaire that takes approximately five minutes to complete. Please comment INTERESTED below or send me a private message, and I'll share the questionnaire link with you. I'd also welcome HR professionals, workplace leaders and others sharing this invitation across their networks. The more experiences we hear, the more informed our conversations can become. Because women's voices need to be part of the conversation about menopause in the workplace. Becoming Her Real Conversations Real Stories Real Women www.nikkitaylor.com.au Becoming Her

Somebody has to ask the obvious question, and apparently that somebody is me, as Beavis is off this week. Always the consummate professional, I reached out to BSO's Carey Codd (Senior Person In Charge of Disinformation) and asked the agency to apply its own criteria to its own boss. Among the questions: Any gang tattoos in this photo? Is the nipple barbell a gang token? If so, how does one tell the filigree from the filigree? Then there's our 911 call center, where civilian operators (typically women … no way! … way!!!) have reportedly been told to expose their chests for a tattoo or jewelry inspection. I asked: Where do these photos end up? A file cabinet, or ratemyrack(dot)com? Was the Sheriff's bosom put through the same inspection? Are boobs fair game, but moobs exempt? Full letter on my Substack. Past or present BSO dispatcher? Drop me a line: [email redacted]. No nudes required.

sports-industry-pros-womens-sport-revenu.core: Posted in last 7 days Sports Industry Pros - Women's Sport Revenue Gap A quick update following on from my last post about The Commercial Dept., the platform I started on the side. Our latest post is out: "Women's sport is booming. So why is the gap still huge?" We look at the records being broken, the athletes and brands changing the game, and the numbers that show how far there still is to go. Women's elite sport is set to pass $3bn in revenue for the first time this year, but that's still only about a third of what the Premier League makes on its own. We also set out what needs to happen to close the gap. Why did I start it? I've always loved the business side of sport. I wanted somewhere to break that down in a simple, honest way, and to shine a light on the people who make it happen. It's a passion project I'm building alongside my career. That's why I launched Inside the Dept., our feature series with people working across the industry. We've got some great people lined up to be featured soon, from all levels and all corners of sport, because every story matters, not just the ones at the top. If you work in sport, whether in partnerships, marketing, retail, wholesale, brand or anything in between, I'd love to hear from you. Whether you'd like to be featured, have an idea for a topic, or just want to chat, please drop me a message. Thank you to everyone who has supported it so far. Plenty more to come. 🙌 #SportsBusiness #Partnerships #SportsMarketing
